newsitem.title: ITALY: Germany's Hax repeats call for EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Hax repeats call for EMU delay.

text.p: Leading German economist Herbert Hax said in an Italian radio interview the start of European economic and monetary union should be delayed by a year and that Germany would probably not meet entry criteria.

Hax, chairman of the council of advisors known as the "five wise men", said in an interview with Milan-based Radio Popolare: "It is necessary to act taking into account the possibility the parameters for the euro might not be met.
"This doesn't mean relaxing the parameters but rather putting off the start of European Union by a year," he said.

Hax, who last weekend called for a delay in the EMU start date, reiterated that Germany would likely miss the government debt/GDP target ratio of 60 percent "and it will also be difficult for Germany to meet the deficit target."

He said he was against a political solution to get EMU under way in 1999, setting aside the economic criteria. "If this happened, monetary union would start off limping and market confidence in the new currency would be seriously undermined.
"Certainly, the danger that this might happen exists," he added.
